title: Command stop-point declarations
description: The `stops:` block a command file carries in its YAML frontmatter. One entry per place the command waits for a human, each naming what happens when nobody answers. Validated per command file: the document is that file's frontmatter reduced to its `stops:` key.

stops.description: Every stop point in this command. A command with no stop point carries no `stops:` key at all rather than an empty list — an empty list reads as 'measured, none found' and would be indistinguishable from a file the scan never opened.

id.description: Stable identity of this stop point, unique within the command. It is what the prose anchor `<!-- stop: <id> -->` names, and what a ledger record or a pending entry binds to. Constrained to a filename- and path-safe alphabet because it becomes both.

class.description:
duplicate — the prompt restated a control the host's permission system and the managed-region guard already apply; it is removed and the command states what it writes instead. risk — a confirmation with an unsafe side (delete, apply, flip). selection — a choice among options with a sane default. knowledge — a question only a human can answer.

`duplicate` is in the enum so the scan has a name for what was removed and can reject a declaration that still carries it; a surviving `duplicate` entry is a scan failure, not a valid declaration.

default.description: The answer taken when nobody answers. Required for risk and selection. Null for knowledge: a knowledge question has no defensible default, and inventing one is the failure this whole declaration exists to prevent.

on_silence.description: What the command does when the session cannot produce a human answer. safe-side — take the non-destructive branch (never delete, never apply, never flip). take-default — take the declared default. refuse — stop before writing anything and list the questions. unanswered — leave the field unanswered in the produced artifact and record it as such.

prompt.description: The question as the command asks it, in one line. This is what a refusal lists and what a pending entry shows, so it has to read as a question to a human, not as an internal key.

options.description: For a selection: the answers on offer. The declared default must be one of them, and an override map may never widen a selection past this list.
